newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND PRAISED BY ALL BLACKS SKIPPER.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-ENGLAND PRAISED BY ALL BLACKS SKIPPER.

text.p: England earned a glowing tribute from All Blacks captain Sean Fitzpatrick after their record 46-6 Five Nations demolition of Ireland at Lansdowne Road on Saturday.

Fitzpatrick, the world's most-capped test forward, is in Britain on a warm-up tour for the forthcoming Super 12 southern hemisphere tournament and was deeply impressed by England's second record points-scoring display in successive matches.
"I thought they were quite outstanding. The sheer power of the English pack amazed me and the three loose forwards had outstanding games.
"As players we're trying to promote the game. That's the sort of rugby people want to watch."
Fitzpatrick led the New Zealand Barbarians team who beat England 34-19 at Twickenham in November. He conceded Phil de Glanville's side had made considerable progress since then.
"They are developing the confidence to have a go. I think you have a team that is going to go on and develop into a very good one.
"The next one (against France) will be the big crunch. It'll be a great game at Twickenham."

Fitzpatrick's Auckland side play Harlequins in London on Tuesday and have also arranged a fixture against newly-crowned European champions Brive next Saturday before flying to South Africa to begin the defence of their Super 12 title.
